evidence: POSIX BRE does not define `\|` as alternation; GNU grep supports it as an extension. macOS ships BSD grep where this extension is absent.

findings.finding: AC 9's proving command uses `grep -rn` with BRE-style grouping `'\(high\|medium\|low\)'`, where `\|` alternation is a GNU extension not present in POSIX BRE. On non-GNU `grep` implementations (macOS default, BSD) this pattern silently fails to match anything, making the 'no matches' result meaningless — a missed fixture would not be detected.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — second-to-last bullet: `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/`
scenarios: CI runs on macOS or an Alpine image with BusyBox grep; the pattern matches nothing in all cases; a surviving `"high"` fixture passes the grep check undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/` with `grep -rEn '"divergent_implementation": "(high|medium|low)"' tests/ src/`.

findings.finding: The schema change (`PlanSeverityAttrs.divergent_implementation` becomes a closed Literal) and the `impact_plan` logic change are acknowledged as breaking, but the plan provides no explicit rollback or back-out path. The T4 rubric requires more than acknowledgement — it requires a reversibility mechanism or expand-contract sequencing. If deployed prompts do not propagate atomically with the schema change, or if the LLM returns old ordinal grades during the deployment window, every plan-review parse will fail with no stated recovery procedure.
findings.location: What §1 (structural changes to `impact_plan`); AC3 (Literal makes `"low"` a parse error); last AC (fixture migration)
scenarios: A prompt cache or model-version issue causes the LLM to return `"high"` for the axis after deployment; every downstream parse fails and plan reviews are fully blocked with no stated recovery path.
A post-deployment defect is found in `impact_plan`; rolling back requires reverting the schema Literal simultaneously, but no rollback procedure is documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider an expand-contract approach: in a first deploy, accept both old (`low|medium|high`) and new (`contradicts_reality|omits_required_site|incomplete_enumeration`) grades with a deprecation log; in a second deploy (after prompt propagation is confirmed), drop old grades. This eliminates the deployment-window risk without a two-version-bump cost.

findings.finding: The plan introduces `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES = ('ac_unverifiable', 'divergent_implementation')` as a new named tuple abstraction that drives both the contribution loop and the override loop, rather than simply mirroring the existing `ac_unverifiable` exclusion pattern already in the code (`if a != 'ac_unverifiable'`). The Rule of Three says generalize at three uses; with only two axes the tuple is a novel architectural pattern. The plan gives no justification for the abstraction over the simpler approach, and introduces a new contract (any future kind-graded axis must be registered in `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES`) that is not recorded in any ADR or design document.

evidence: Plan asserts compat: 'legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error'
Plan also asserts new Literal makes '"low"|"medium"|"high" a parse error' (AC line re fixture migration)
No mechanism is named for reconciling these two requirements (e.g., version-discriminated model classes, a pre-parse coercion shim, Union type with tagged discriminator, or silent-unknown handling)
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error' but does not specify the mechanism that allows existing corpus entries carrying `divergent_implementation: "high"` (or `"low"`/`"medium"`) to be parsed through a model whose Literal now rejects those values. A naive Literal change would cause a parse error on every historical sidecar record that holds an ordinal grade.
findings.location: AC: '`IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` is bumped to `plan-v4`, and legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error. Verified: `test_impact_model_versioning.py` pins updated and green.'
scenarios: A corpus-replay calibration run (one of the two permitted A/B forms per the new ADR 0054) reads plan-v3 sidecars containing `divergent_implementation: "high"` through the updated model and raises ValidationError, aborting the replay entirely.
Any monitoring or analytics path that deserialises the full corpus post-deploy breaks silently or noisily on the ~7.72% of plan-v3 findings where the axis was graded non-`none`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a version-discriminated schema approach: keep a `PlanSeverityAttrsV3` model (or a `Annotated[Union[...], Discriminator(...)]`) that accepts the old ordinal grades, and route deserialisation through it when the sidecar's `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` tag is `plan-v3` or `plan-v2`. Reference this in the AC verification step so the test actually exercises the cross-version path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the post-rollback schema state explicitly: either (a) plan-v4 findings are forward-compatible with plan-v3 readers (specify how), or (b) a compensating-forward migration quarantines/re-grades plan-v4 findings before rollback, and attach a `DATA LOSS RISK` note if partial failure could drop findings.
evidence: Plan states the version bump 'closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort' — implying new findings are written immediately after deploy
No rollback procedure is described for the IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump or the Literal change
T11 POST-ROLLBACK SCHEMA STATE requirement: 'the plan must assert on the schema STATE AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback exits 0'
ABSENCE: no mention of compensating-forward strategy, corpus quarantine of plan-v4 findings, or forward-compat shim in plan-v3 code
findings.finding: The plan does not assert the schema state AFTER a rollback of plan-v4. Any findings written to the corpus with new grade strings (`contradicts_reality`, `omits_required_site`, `incomplete_enumeration`) before a rollback would be unreadable by reverted plan-v3 code, yet the plan offers no back-out path or DATA LOSS RISK acknowledgement for this window.
findings.location: Section 'What' / version-bump description; Out-of-scope section; no rollback section exists in the plan.
scenarios: Plan-v4 is deployed; 200 new findings are written with `divergent_implementation: "omits_required_site"`. A regression is discovered and plan-v3 code is restored. Those 200 corpus entries now fail to deserialise, breaking corpus replay and any analytics that touch them.
A partial deploy (e.g., only the schema change is live, not the impact_plan logic) writes plan-v4 findings that the partially-rolled-back reader cannot parse.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure AC-6 (or a dedicated AC) explicitly requires the verifier prompt block for `divergent_implementation` to include a non-flooring coaching guard for `incomplete_enumeration` analogous to the `underspecified_oracle` guard at `plan_review_verifier.md:78-80`, and extend the grep verify to confirm its presence (e.g. `grep -c 'incomplete_enumeration.*coached\|never floors' plan_review_verifier*.md` returns >=1 per file).
evidence: Current prompt for ac_unverifiable includes the explicit coaching guard (plan_review_verifier.md:78-80): 'HARD-OVERRIDE for missing_oracle and broken_oracle ONLY (auto-high). underspecified_oracle is a coached refinement: it scores BELOW every blocking threshold and never floors — do not use a floor grade for a specificity demand.'

Plan What §1 specifies that incomplete_enumeration is the 'pressure-release valve' and 'never floors', but AC-6's grep verify (`grep -c "omits_required_site"... returns at least 1`) does not verify that the non-flooring coaching guard is present in the prompt.
Without this guard in the prompt, verifier LLMs may over-apply `omits_required_site` to cosmetic omissions, replicating the over-firing the three-way split was designed to prevent.
findings.finding: The verifier prompts' new `divergent_implementation` block (as prescribed) will carry a non-flooring/coached rule for `incomplete_enumeration` analogous to the `underspecified_oracle` rule in `ac_unverifiable`, but neither the plan nor the AC set specifies that this decision rule — 'incomplete_enumeration is below every blocking threshold and never floors; do not use it as a floor grade' — must appear in the prompt body co-located with the grade definitions, leaving the enforcement signal absent from the LLM's instruction set.
findings.location: AC-6; plan What §1 ('incomplete_enumeration ... Contributes DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, BELOW every blocking threshold, and NEVER floors — coached, not auto-blocked'); src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md:78-80 (the analogous ac_unverifiable rule present in current prompts)
scenarios: LLM verifier applies `omits_required_site` to a docs-only omission because the prompt lists the grade but does not caution 'use incomplete_enumeration for optional/cosmetic omissions'; the 0.85 floor fires on a coached finding, defeating the split's purpose.
A future prompt update copies the grade vocabulary without the decision rule; the code-level floor logic is correct but the LLM grading is unconstrained.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the divergent_implementation block in both prompts: 'HARD-OVERRIDE for contradicts_reality and omits_required_site ONLY (auto-high, 0.85 floor). incomplete_enumeration is a coached refinement: it scores BELOW every blocking threshold and never floors — do not use a floor grade when the omitted site is optional or cosmetic.' Then verify with grep.

findings.finding: The prompts' preamble instruction — 'Grade each axis none|low|medium|high (EXCEPT ac_unverifiable, which uses its own oracle-kind grades below)' — will become a pink-elephant antipattern after the change: it implicitly tells the verifier LLM that divergent_implementation is still on the ordinal ladder. The plan specifies no AC check that this preamble exception list is updated to also exclude divergent_implementation.
findings.location: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md line 65; src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md line 71; Acceptance Criteria bullet 6
findings.suggested_fix: Update the preamble in both prompt files from 'EXCEPT ac_unverifiable, which uses its own oracle-kind grades below' to 'EXCEPT ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation, which each use their own closed kind sets below'. Add a grep check in AC bullet 6 such as: `grep -c "EXCEPT ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md` returns >= 1 per file.

findings.finding: tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py uses "divergent_implementation": "high" (lines 113, 122, 124) and is not listed as an edit target. After the Literal constraint is added (AC3) and divergent_implementation is excluded from _SEV01 (structural change 3), "high" is out-of-vocabulary and maps to 0.0 in DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, causing impact_plan(attrs) to return < 0.85 and the test at line 124 to fail.
findings.location: AC3 (Literal schema change) + AC4 (DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 structural changes) / tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py lines 113-124
findings.suggested_fix: In test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py lines 113-124, replace `"divergent_implementation": "high"` with `"divergent_implementation": "omits_required_site"` and update the assertion at line 122 to match.

findings.finding: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py uses "divergent_implementation": "high" (line 1282) as a hard-override fixture to drive a BLOCK decision, and is not listed as an edit target. After the structural changes in AC3/AC4, "high" is invalid and maps to 0.0, so the negative-control test that depends on impact_plan returning a high score will silently break.
findings.location: AC3 + AC4 / tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py line 1282

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit `enrich_operator_attested` changes sub-section (or bullet) to What §1 describing the unconditional `incomplete_enumeration`→`none` mapping on attestation and the floor-grade pass-through rule, so the deliverable is covered in both body and AC.
evidence: What §1 enumerates four named structural changes: DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, _DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES, _PLAN_GRADED_AXES loop unification, and the hard-override check replacement — all in `impact_plan`. `enrich_operator_attested` is not named anywhere in the What section.

AC 8 specifies: 'MUST set `incomplete_enumeration` to `none` (automatic, not discretionary)' and 'MUST NOT alter `contradicts_reality` or `omits_required_site`' — a distinct functional requirement with no corresponding body description.
findings.finding: The What section describes no work on `enrich_operator_attested`, yet the AC requires a non-trivial, unconditional behavioral change to that function (attestation must set `incomplete_enumeration`→`none` and must NOT alter floor grades). An implementer reading only What §1 would have no signal that `enrich_operator_attested` must be touched, making this an orphan criterion with no covering description.
findings.location: AC line 8 ('enrich_operator_attested handling is explicit and UNCONDITIONAL…') vs. What §1 (four named structural changes, all in `impact_plan`)
scenarios: An implementer implements all four named `impact_plan` structural changes and all ADR work but never opens `enrich_operator_attested`, causing the attestation AC to fail at review time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet under What §1: '5. Update `enrich_operator_attested` to handle the new grades unconditionally: map `incomplete_enumeration` → `"none"` on any recorded operator attestation (automatic, not discretionary); leave `contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site` unchanged, mirroring the existing `broken_oracle` rule.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit prompt-update deliverable to What §1 (or §2) describing: (a) add a `divergent_implementation` kind-grade block with worked examples for all three grades to both verifier prompts, matching the `ac_unverifiable` block shape; and (b) update the shared preamble to name both `ac_unverifiable` and `divergent_implementation` as kind-graded axes.
evidence: What §1 describes four structural changes all within `impact_plan` source code, plus the ADR. No sentence says 'update `plan_review_verifier.md` and `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`.'

The body's only prompt reference is the precedent phrase: 'Mirror the oracle-kind precedent exactly' and a parenthetical '(worked examples in story large-sleepful-needlefish)' — neither of which constitutes a deliverable description.
AC6 specifies concrete verify commands against the prompt files; the preamble AC specifies a grep against the preamble line — two distinct deliverables with zero body coverage.
findings.finding: The verifier-prompt updates (grade definitions + worked examples for all three new grades, and the preamble change removing the ordinal-ladder mention) are substantive deliverables covered by two ACs (AC6 and the preamble AC) but are not described as explicit work items in the What section. An implementer reading only the What section would infer at most that prompts 'should' be updated by analogy, with no actionable description of what to write.
findings.location: AC6 ('Both verifier prompts define all three grades with a worked example each…') and the preamble AC ('…line names BOTH kind-graded axes') vs. What §1 (no prompt-update bullet)
scenarios: An implementer finishes all four `impact_plan` structural changes and the ADR but treats the prompt files as out-of-scope because the What section never lists them, causing two ACs to fail.
